target_source.text: Upon approaching an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency which is moving or preparing to move in any direction, including, without limitation, arriving at or leaving the scene of a crash or other incident, and making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3], the driver of any other vehicle shall, except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer: If the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of a regulatory agency: (1) Approaches the driver’s vehicle, proceed as required pursuant to subsection 1 [NRS-484B-267-1a, NRS-484B-267-1b, NRS-484B-267-1c]; or (2) Stops, proceed as required pursuant to NRS 484B.607 [NRS-484B-607-1a, NRS-484B-607-1b, NRS-484B-607-1c, NRS-484B-607-1d]. As used in this section, “preparing to move” means any indication that is visible to an approaching driver that an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency is about to move, including, without limitation: (a) A movement of the vehicle; or (b) The use of hand signals by the driver of the vehicle.

supplied_same_cell_sources.text: Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency, making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3], the driver of every other vehicle shall, except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer: Yield the right-of-way.

Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency, making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3], the driver of every other vehicle shall, except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer: Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph, immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway and clear of any intersection. The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder. The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency, making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3], the driver of every other vehicle shall, except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer: Stop and remain in such position until the authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle has passed.

approaches_referral.measurement_boundary: Observe source-bound approach, yield, right-edge clearance and stop-until-passed separately; physical and legal outcomes require original review.

stops_referral.measurement_boundary: Measure the stop and route the case to NRS 484B.607. Do not infer the unsupplied 607 duties or a compliance verdict.

activation: authorized emergency or regulatory-agency official vehicle
moving or visibly preparing to move
alternatives: emergency or official vehicle approaches the subject
exceptions: otherwise directed by law enforcement officer
preparation_indicators: visible hand signal by its driver
